en.text: Derivative = gradient of the tangent = instantaneous rate of change. Rules: power, sum, constant multiple, product, quotient, chain. Uses: tangents and normals, increasing/decreasing, maxima and minima, rates and optimisation. Integration reverses differentiation: ∫ from a to b of f dx = F(b) − F(a), the net area.

screens.title: Key words
defs: f′(a): the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).
The exact area under f from a to b: the limit of the Riemann sums.

screens.title: Match the idea
screens.why:
f′ goes + to −: rising then falling, a hill → relative maximum.
f′ goes − to +: falling then rising, a valley → relative minimum.
f′(c) = 0 or undefined (c in the domain) → c is a critical number.
F(b) − F(a) → the definite integral from a to b.
−1/f′(a) → the slope of the normal (perpendicular to the tangent).
screens.text: Unit 2 key facts: match each fact with its name.
Derivative or integral? Sort each task by the tool it needs.
items: slope of the tangent at x = 2
total cost from marginal cost C′(x)
screens.why:
Derivatives go from a total to a rate (slope, velocity, marginal).
Integrals go from a rate back to a total (area, distance, total cost).
They undo each other: that is the Fundamental Theorem.
screens.clue: Are you going from a total to a rate, or from a rate to a total?

screens.ask: Derivative at a point (simplify first): f(x) = (x³ + 3x)/x². f′(2) = ___
screens.why:
Divide each term by x²: f(x) = x + 3/x = x + 3x⁻¹.
f′(x) = 1 − 3x⁻² = 1 − 3/x².
f′(2) = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.
The quotient rule gives the same, with more work.

screens.ask: Velocity of a falling object: height y = 80 − 4.9t² (m). Its velocity at t = 1 s is ___ m/s
screens.why:
Velocity = dy/dt.
dy/dt = 0 − 9.8t = −9.8t.
At t = 1: −9.8 m/s.
The minus sign means the height is falling.

screens.ask: Optimisation: a farmer has 240 m of fence for a field by a river (no fence on the river side). The largest area = ___ m²
screens.why:
Let x = each side at right angles to the river; the far side is 240 − 2x.
A = x(240 − 2x) = 240x − 2x².
A′ = 240 − 4x = 0 gives x = 60.
A′ goes + to −: a maximum.
A = 60 × 120 = 7200 m².
Trap: a square 80 × 80 = 6400 is not the best here.
screens.clue: Two sides x and one side 240 − 2x.

items.text: Slope of a secant: y = 1/x from x = 3 to x = 3 + Δx. The slope is
items.why:
Slope = (1/(3 + Δx) − 1/3)/Δx.
Common denominator: (3 − (3 + Δx))/(3(3 + Δx)) = −Δx/(3(3 + Δx)).
Divide by Δx: −1/(3(3 + Δx)) = −1/(9 + 3Δx).
−1/9 is the limit as Δx → 0 (the tangent slope), not the secant slope.

items.ask: Average speed: distance y = t² (m). Average speed from t = 2 to t = 2.1 is ___ m/s
items.why:
Average speed = (y(2.1) − y(2))/(2.1 − 2).
y(2.1) = 4.41 and y(2) = 4.
(4.41 − 4)/0.1 = 0.41/0.1 = 4.1 m/s.
Check: close to the instant speed y′(2) = 4.

x³(1 − 1/x) = x³ − x².
(x³ − x²)(x² − 1/x²) = x⁵ − x − x⁴ + 1.
So f(x) = x⁵ − x⁴ − x + 1.
f′(x) = 5x⁴ − 4x³ − 1.

items.text: Increasing and decreasing: f(x) = 6x⁵ − 50x³ − 120 is decreasing on
items.why:
f′(x) = 30x⁴ − 150x² = 30x²(x² − 5).
30x² ≥ 0 always, so the sign comes from x² − 5.
x² − 5 ≤ 0 when −√5 ≤ x ≤ √5.
So f is decreasing on [−√5, √5].
On (−∞, −√5] and [√5, ∞) it is increasing.

items.text: Related rates: on the curve 2y = x² + 4, where does y change 4 times as fast as x?
items.why:
Differentiate with respect to t: 2 dy/dt = 2x dx/dt.
So dy/dt = x dx/dt.
We want dy/dt = 4 dx/dt, so x = 4.
y = (16 + 4)/2 = 10. The point is (4, 10).

items.text: Extreme value conditions: f(x) = x² + px + q has an extreme value f(1) = 3. Find p and q.
items.why:
At an extreme value, f′(1) = 0.
f′(x) = 2x + p, so 2 + p = 0 and p = −2.
f(1) = 1 + p + q = 3, so 1 − 2 + q = 3 and q = 4.
Answer: p = −2, q = 4.

items.ask: Related rates (sliding board): a 5 ft board slides down a wall. The bottom is 4 ft from the wall; the top moves down 2 ft/s. The bottom slides out at ___ ft/s
items.why:
Pythagoras: x² + y² = 25. At x = 4, y = 3.
Differentiate: 2x dx/dt + 2y dy/dt = 0.
The top moves down, so dy/dt = −2.
4 dx/dt + 3(−2) = 0, so dx/dt = 6/4 = 1.5 ft/s.

items.ask: Related rates for a sphere: a balloon's radius grows 0.5 cm/s. At r = 4 cm, the surface area grows ___π cm²/s
items.why:
S = 4πr².
dS/dt = 8πr dr/dt.
dS/dt = 8π(4)(0.5) = 16π cm²/s.
So the blank is 16.

items.ask: Distance as an area: a cyclist slows steadily from 30 km/h to 0 in 45 s. The distance covered is ___ m
items.why:
Change units first: 30 km/h = 30 000 m ÷ 3600 s = 25/3 m/s.
The v–t graph is a straight line from 25/3 down to 0: a triangle.
Area = (1/2)(45)(25/3) = 187.5 m.
Trap: mixing km/h with seconds gives a wrong number.

items.ask: Total from a rate: pollution N′(t) = 280t^(3/2) lb per month. The total in the first 16 months is ___ lb

items.text: The product of two positive numbers is 100 such that the sum of two times the first number and eight times the second number is minimum. Which one of the following pairs of numbers are the first and the second numbers respectively?
items.why:
Let the numbers be x and y, with xy = 100, so y = 100/x.
Sum to minimise: S(x) = 2x + 8y = 2x + 800/x.
S′(x) = 2 − 800/x² = 0 gives x² = 400, x = 20 (x > 0).
y = 100/20 = 5. S″(x) = 1600/x³ > 0: a minimum, S = 80.
Check: (25, 4) gives 82, (50, 2) gives 116; (1, 99) has product 99, not 100.

items.text: The maximum profit that a company can make if the profit function is given by P(x) = 36 + 72x − 18x² is ____.
items.why:
P′(x) = 72 − 36x = 0 gives x = 2.
P″(x) = −36 < 0, so x = 2 is a maximum.
P(2) = 36 + 144 − 72 = 108.
Trap: 2 is the best x, not the profit.

items.text: If the perimeter of a rectangle is 120 m, what are the length l and width w maximizing its area?
Let f(x) = 1/√x and g(x) = 2 − (1/6)x³ be two functions. For what value of x do the graphs of f and g have tangent lines with the same slope?
Which of the following describes the mechanical meaning of the derivative?
opts: B. Gradient of graph of functions
items.why:
Mechanical (physical) meaning: the instantaneous rate of change.
Example: velocity is the rate of change of position.
B and C are the geometric meaning: the slope of the tangent.
A, the area under a curve, is the meaning of a definite integral.

items.text: Let f and g be differentiable functions and h(x) = g(f(3x + 1)). If f′(1) = f(1) = 2 and g′(2) = 1, then what is the value of h′(0)?

test.why:
(x⁴)′ = 4x³ (power rule).
(3x)′ = 3.
Answer: 4x³ − 3.
Trap: 4x³ − 3x forgets to differentiate 3x.

test.ask: Derivative at a point: f(x) = x³ − 3x². f′(1) = ___
Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from 0 to 2 (3x² + 2x) dx = ___
Relative minimum value: f(x) = x³ − 12x. The relative minimum value is ___
test.why:
f′(x) = 3x² − 12 = 0 gives x = ±2.
f′ goes − to + at x = 2: a minimum.
f(2) = 8 − 24 = −16.
Trap: x = 2 is where it happens; the value is −16.

f′(x) = 3(2x − 1)² × 2 (outside, then inside).
f′(1) = 3(1)²(2) = 6.
Trap: 3 forgets the inner derivative 2.
